title: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience
description: Nanoscape: The Journal for Undergraduate Research in Nanoscience is an annual publication of original research conducted by undergraduates from around the county. The journal was launched in 2004 and was the first of its kind in the country. The journal disseminates the results of undergraduate research in the broad fields of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Nanoscape is an educational outreach project of the Northwestern University Nanoscale Science and Engineering Center (NSEC), which is part of the International Institute for Nanotechnology (IIN), both of which are under the direction of Professor Chad A. Mirkin. This work was supported primarily by the Nanoscale Science and Engineering Initiative of the National Science Foundation Under NSF award number EEC–0755375 AND EEC-0647560.

title: DNA Surface Characterization Using Second Harmonic Generation and Contact-Angle Goniometry
creator: Boyee Wong
description:
Chip-based devices and biosensors
incorporate the attachment of biomolecules
at interfaces. The behavior of biomolecules
at the surface and interfaces differs from the
behavior of biomolecules in the bulk solution.
Surface-analysis techniques are therefore
required to characterize these interfaces.
Second harmonic generation (SHG) has been
used to characterize DNA on a quartz lens to
model biomolecules at the surface.
Optimization of the surface-attachment
procedure using contact-angle goniometry is
necessary to optimize the results of laser
experiments. Contact-angle goniometry is
used to optimize surface preparation
parameters, such as concentration of NHS,
concentration of water, reaction time, and
various cleaning strategies. Studying DNA
surfaces can assist with improvements in
DNA detection systems for biodiagnostics by
determining important structural information
about the biomolecules.
